# Screen Walk

> Screen Walk is an iPhone app that keeps blocking the apps and websites you choose, using Apple's Screen Time technology. Walking tops up minutes on a transit-style fare card, and you start a timed break of 5 to 60 minutes by pressing and holding the card on a reader. Blocking returns by itself when the break ends.

Facts
- Platform: iPhone (iOS). The interface is English only. Version 1.4.0. Made by one independent developer.
- Pace: by default 250 steps top up 1 minute; the pace can be set from 100 to 1,000 steps a minute, in steps of 50.
- Steps come from Apple Health (a phone in a pocket or an Apple Watch).
- Minutes you don't use carry over into tomorrow, then drop off the card.
- Blocking hours (new in 1.4.0): blocking can run all the time (the default) or only on the days and hours you pick. Outside those hours the apps are open and no minutes are used.
- Emergency break: a 5-minute break that uses no minutes; one a day by default, 0 to 3 can be chosen.
- Turning blocking off is deliberate and delayed: a long hold in Settings, then it takes effect at a coming midnight at least 12 hours away, and can be cancelled until then.
- Price: 7 free days, then one payment. No subscription and nothing renews. $9.99 in the United States; other countries see their local price in the app.
- Privacy: no account, no ads. Step counts, Health data and the chosen apps stay on the phone. The app sends anonymous usage events to its own server.
- It is for your own use, not a parental control app.
- No streaks, no nagging notifications.
